taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_typical_m.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 255, Lomatium utriculatum: "Plants caulescent, 1-5 dm. tall, glabrous to pubescent, from a long slender taproot".

traits.inflorescence_branches.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 255, Lomatium utriculatum: "rays 5-13, spreading to ascending, un- equal, 1-12 cm. long".

traits.inflorescence.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 255, Lomatium utriculatum: rays 5-13, each ending in an umbellet on pedicels "2-9 mm. long": a compound umbel.

traits.leaf_division.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 255, Lomatium utriculatum: "Leaves tripinnate, sometimes ternate, then tripinnate".

traits.division_pattern.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 255, Lomatium utriculatum: "Leaves tripinnate, sometimes ternate, then tripinnate".

traits.division_order.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 255, Lomatium utriculatum: "Leaves tripinnate, sometimes ternate, then tripinnate".

traits.pinnae.note: Seven primary divisions, set by hand from general knowledge of the species: Abrams (1951 p. 255) gives no count.

traits.leaflets.note: Five divisions to each primary division, set by hand from general knowledge of the species: Abrams (1951 p. 255) gives no count.

traits.terminal_leaflet.note: Odd-pinnate, each division ending in one, set by hand: Abrams (1951 p. 255) does not say.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 255, Lomatium utriculatum: "leaf-divisions linear, 2-25 mm. long".

traits.leaflet_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 255, Lomatium utriculatum: "leaf-divisions linear, 2-25 mm. long".

traits.flower_colour.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 255, Lomatium utriculatum: "flowers yellow"; sRGB by eye.

traits.fruit_size_m.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 255, Lomatium utriculatum: "fruit ovate to oblong, 5-11 mm. long".

traits.flowering_months.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 255, Lomatium utriculatum: "Grassy hillsides and plains" ... "March-June".

traits.life_span.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 255, Lomatium utriculatum: perennial from "a long slender taproot".

appearance.organs.flower.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 255, Lomatium utriculatum: rays "spreading to ascending, un- equal, 1-12 cm. long"; pedicels "2-9 mm. long"; "flowers yellow". Drawn as 9 rays of up to about 6 cm, each ending in an umbellet of 10 small yellow flowers about 1 cm across.

generator.params.note: Pacific water parsley's values, changed by hand for common lomatium: a few low stems from a taproot, their finely divided leaves largest near the base, each stem ending in a yellow compound umbel (Abrams 1951 p. 255). Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: 0.3 m tall at 4 years in the open, the middle of Abrams's 1-5 dm. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: By eye, after Abrams (1951 p. 255): yellow flowers; green, finely dissected leaves.
